We have template details. The retro_smarts_template is the retrosynthetic direction (product -> precursors). The mapped_rxn shows forward reaction? Actually mapped_rxn shows forward? It shows reactants -> product? It shows ([CH3:1]/[C:2]... )>> product. That's forward. The retro template is reverse.

Our target molecule is the product side of the retro reaction (i.e., the complex molecule). The retro template should match product to give precursors. The retro_smarts_template is:

'[C:8]-[C@@H;D3;+0:9](-[C@H;D3;+0:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12])-[C@;H0;D4;+0:2](-[C:1])(-[OH;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7])>>[C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7]).[C:8]/[CH;D2;+0:9]=[C;H0;D3;+0:10](/[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12]'

So product side is left side? Actually retro_smarts_template: left side is product (complex) and right side is precursors (two fragments). So applying retro template to our molecule should give two fragments: fragment A: [C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;...])-[C:4]... and fragment B: [C:8]/[CH;...]=... etc.

Our apply_template call used template_id 1914384 but returned empty. Possibly because our molecule SMILES includes atom mapping numbers that don't match the template's mapping indices. The template expects certain atom map numbers (1-...?). Our molecule mapping uses 1-18 but template uses 1-15 maybe. The mapping numbers need to align? The apply_template likely matches based on substructure ignoring mapping? Not sure.

We could try without mapping: remove atom map tags. Provide SMILES without mapping. Let's generate unmapped SMILES: The given is "[CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]". Remove the ":n" parts. That yields "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CC C C1(O)C(F)(F)F"? Let's construct: CH2= C( aromatic ) C@@H1 CH2 CH2 CH2 C@@1(OH) C(F)(F)F. So SMILES: "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CC C C1O C(F)(F)F"? Need correct: CH2= C( c1ccccc1 ) C1CC C C1(O)C(F)(F)F. So "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CC C C1O C(F)(F)F". Actually need proper: "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CC C C1O C(F)(F)F". Let's write: "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CC C C1O C(F)(F)F". Might be "C= C(c1ccccc1)C1CC C C1O C(F)(F)F". Let's just try apply_template with unmapped SMILES.
